- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- If model shows sharp upward spike after recent low, often overshoots; cap peak forecast at 1.5–2x recent high or use moving average to smooth.  
- When sentiment turns positive after prolonged negative streak, model often underreacts; increase forecast slope gently to reflect sentiment shift.  
- Model frequently underestimates mean reversion in short-term (1–3d) after sharp moves; add 0.5–1.0% buffer to forecast if recent price moved >3% in 1d.  
- For 30d horizon, model often overestimates volatility in early forecast window; reduce first 5–7 days’ forecast by 0.5–1.5% if sentiment is neutral or mildly negative.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., -0.5 → +0.3 → -0.4), model tends to lag; add 1–2 day lag correction to forecast peak.  
- When sentiment is flat or mildly positive, model often overestimates upside; cap forecast at 1.2x recent 7d average if sentiment > -0.2.
